ev.q: In 2012, a total of 9,951 new tuberculosis (TB) cases were reported in the United States, an incidence of 3.2 cases per 100,000 population
The TB rate among foreign-born persons in the United States in 2012 was 11.5 times higher than among U.S.-born persons.
The incidence decreased to 3.2 cases per 100,000 population from 3.4 in 2011
Among those with a known result, 7.7% were reported as HIV-positive.

From 2011 to 2012, TB rates per 100,000 population decreased most for Hispanics (9.1%), followed by blacks (7.4%)
The TB rate among foreign-born persons in the United States in 2012 was 11.5 times higher than among U.S.-born persons.
The TB rate among U.S.-born blacks was 5.8 times greater than for U.S.-born whites
This report summarizes provisional TB surveillance data reported to CDC's National Tuberculosis Surveillance System in 2012.

methods_quotes.q: CDC calculates national and state TB rates overall and by racial/ethnic group, using U.S. Census Bureau population estimates
The Current Population Survey provides the population denominators used to calculate TB rates and percentage changes
case rates are calculated from estimates, not counts, of population denominators from 2012
